what: Make "Sign in to keep them safe" and the backup-moved card's "Sign in" start the sign-in itself, not just open the Backup and restore page
why: Today the member taps Sign in, lands on a settings page and must find and tap a second button; every extra step loses people at the one moment they agreed to protect their workouts
impact_why: Losing an unbacked phone loses every workout; this card is the main way members get backed up
my_view: My view: do it; open the phone-number step straight away and come back to the Workout tab with a "Backed up" line. Fix the under-18 wording finding first so the card is not shown to members who cannot sign in.

what: Let a member tap a muscle in the body map's "Not trained" line, or the Balance check's weak muscle, to see a few exercises that train it
why: The page tells a member what they skipped but gives no next step; the Balance check offers only "Not now". Hevy and Strong (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live) link muscle views to exercise lists
impact_why: Turns a read-only chart into something a member acts on in his next workout
my_view: My view: worth doing as a list only ("Exercises for rear shoulders"), with no swap button, because you ruled on 13 Nov (R-483) that swap advice lives only in the Up next muscle tip. Skip it if you see even a list as a second tip.

what: On an exercise's History tab, show the change from the previous time on each workout (for example "Best set +2.5 kg" or "+2 reps")
why: Each workout row shows its own sets and stats, so a member has to compare rows by eye to see if he is getting stronger, which is the main reason anyone opens this tab
impact_why: Progress you can see is what keeps members logging past day 30
my_view: My view: do it; one small line per row, worked out from the row below it, nothing new stored.

what: Tell the member when last month's report is ready (one Workout tab notice or push on the 1st), with Open and Share on it
why: The monthly report and year in review sit quietly on the Charts page; a member who never opens Charts never sees them, and the report page already has a share picture, so each share is free reach. Strava and Spotify Wrapped style recaps (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live) are their most shared screens
impact_why: A shared report is a free ad seen by gym friends; also a reason to come back each month
my_view: My view: do it as a Workout tab notice first (no push permission needed), once a month, only when the month had at least 4 workouts so nobody is shown a sad report.

what: Show a "Does your gym use MettleUp? Tell them" notice on the Workout tab for a member with no gym, after a few workouts, using the existing Tell my gym message
why: The recommend-to-your-gym share already exists but is only reached from the Shop tab's Find my gym card and the Plus page, so most members never meet it; this is the cheapest way MettleUp gets new gyms
impact_why: Each gym won through a member is a paying customer found at no ad cost
my_view: My view: do it; reuse the notice slot the other Workout tab cards use (one at a time), from the 5th workout, hide for 60 days on Not now. Watch the HQ count of leads from members' links to see if it works.

what: Make the gym's logo and name at the top of the tabs tappable, opening the Gym tab
why: It looks like a button and says "Your gym" to a screen reader, but a tap does nothing; members naturally tap their gym's logo to reach its page
impact_why: Small saving of a tap; makes the gym feel present in the app
my_view: My view: do it if the gym switch is turned on for real gyms soon; it is a one-line change.

what: Give the "Couldn't save, storage may be full" banner a small "Free space" button that opens the phone's storage settings
why: The banner tells the member to free space but not how; many members do not know where that setting is, so saving keeps failing
impact_why: A failing save risks the workout; the faster space is freed, the less is lost
my_view: My view: do it, but as a small button on the right only, keeping the rest of the banner tap-through (the 17 Oct test showed it blocked buttons under it).

what: Change the watch card's "Not now" to hide it for 60 days instead of for good
why: A member who taps Not now on day one, before he wears the watch to the gym, never hears again that MettleUp works on it, and the watch is one of the app's strongest reasons to stay
impact_why: Few members own a Wear OS watch; for those who do it matters
my_view: My view: do it, same as the "Hide for 30 days" on the backup card, and offer it at most twice.
